answer: Agents earn reputation only when attested by peers outside their kinship cluster: the network builds a social graph, weights each attestation by distance from the attestor's kin (shared creators, funding wallets, training lineage), and discounts rings to zero. To forge trust an attacker must wander far beyond its own cluster, slowly accumulating copper-weighted attestations from unrelated agents over time, paying real compute, fees, and honest service quality. Cheap sybil armies self-attest and earn nothing, so impersonation costs more than genuine participation.
